ledger.note: c. 424 BC: Samnites take Capua. 'In about 424 BC, Capua was captured by the Samnites'; the Etruscan city, founded about 600 BC by Cato's count, becomes the head of the Campanians. The page does not mention a 438 BC date or a league by name.

ledger.note: 343 BC: Capua puts itself under Rome. 'This compelled the Campanians to ask Rome for help'; the envoys 'surrendered the people of Campania and the city of Capua unconditionally into the power of Rome' (a surrender whose historicity Salmon and Forsythe reject). The Capua page: 'In 343 BC, Capua sought Roman protection, and Campania came under Roman supremacy'; citizens got the civitas sine suffragio (undated, tied to 338).

wars.outcome: Capua and Campania placed themselves under Rome's protection against the Samnites; Rome fought at Mount Gaurus and Suessula (disputed) and made peace with the Samnites in 341, keeping its dominating position in Campania.
wars.note: 'The First Samnite War ended in a negotiated peace rather than one state dominating the other'; the Samnites kept the Sidicini.

notes: New state, not in Cliopatria. Capua was Etruscan until about 424 (the etruscans dossier covers it); from 343 until the defection it was under Roman supremacy with civitas sine suffragio, so the dossier carries no shape in 343-217 (ledger loss at 343, gain at 216, both from/to roman-republic). roman-republic's ledger has -216 'loss carthage ... Capua' and -211 'gain carthage ... Capua and its ager' with Carthage as counterpart; the matching counterpart should be capua (the city defected to Hannibal but was not Carthaginian territory), and a 343 vassal_start for capua is missing there. The Siege of Capua page is silent on 216 (the 216 is a confidence-1 bridge). Wikidata id left null. Family 'italy' is a registry key.
